scope: Proposition 6.3 (Uniform collision bound) of the manuscript “The sharp terminal leave in random triangle removal” (preprints/The-Sharp-Terminal-Leave-in-Random-Triangle-Removal-September-25-2026/The-Sharp-Terminal-Leave-in-Random-Triangle-Removal-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 188 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 85fbaba652137663), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix k ∈ {1, 2} and sample k independent uniform oriented edges of G, with replacement. Execute the independent root queries at threshold 1, executing every root regardless of earlier outputs. Let Ck be the event that an actual triangle type is repeated among all exposed candidate lists, including candidates not traversed. Then Pind(Ck) = O(D15−B + n−1 ) = O(D−35 + n−1 ) = o(D−1 ). (6.12) The bound is uniform over the graphs in Proposition 2.2. Consequently, by Lemma 5.1, the probabilities that all root queries return true in the finite and independent experiments differ by at most the same bound.
